papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning Kernel Training for Classification Tasks
papers.what_it_is: A simulation benchmark of quantum kernel estimation and quantum kernel training against SVM and logistic regression on artificial and reference classification datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that quantum kernel methods outperformed classical methods on the ad-hoc datasets and gave varying performance across datasets, with the quantum advantage vanishing on the classical datasets.
quotes: Experimental results indicate that quantum methods exhibit varying performance
Perhaps unsurprisingly, quantum methods outperformed classical
The quantum suitability nevertheless vanishes for the subset of classical datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study. Results come from classical simulation of small datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that their experiments call into question a general added value of quantum kernel training, because the added computational cost does not necessarily give better classification performance.
quotes: Our experiments call into question a general added value of applying QKT optimization
the results of our benchmarking call into question a generalized added value of applying QKT optimization.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: This bears on whether trained quantum kernels justify their cost on non-contrived data.

assertions.value: The authors report that quantum kernel training slightly improved results for the Covariant mapping and had a downgrading effect for the ZZ feature maps.
quotes: Whereas QKT seemed to contribute to an overall slight improvement for the Covariant mapping, a downgrading effect was observed for the ZZ- feature maps.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the benchmark runs classical simulations on small, artificial and reference classification datasets, so it does not test real quantum hardware.
quotes: benchmarking models via classical simulations on small, but heterogeneous, and still challenging
benchmarking is performed that involves different artificial and small-scale reference classification datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.

papers.title_in_file: An Expressive Ansatz for Low-Depth Quantum Approximate Optimisation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract and conclusion read in full; body sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Introduces XQAOA, an overparameterised QAOA variant with a Pauli-Y mixer component, and benchmarks it at unit depth on MaxCut against QAOA, MA-QAOA, a Classical-Relaxed algorithm and Goemans-Williamson.

assertions.value: The authors report that at unit depth XQAOA outperforms QAOA, MA-QAOA and the Classical-Relaxed algorithm on all tested unweighted regular graphs with 128 and 256 nodes and degrees from 3 to 10, and outperforms Goemans-Williamson on instances with degrees greater than 4.
quotes: a set of unweighted regular graphs with 128 and 256 nodes for degrees ranging from 3 to 10
allowing it to consistently outperform QAOA, MA-QAOA, and the Classical-Relaxed algorithm
graph instances with degrees greater than 4
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study. MaxCut on regular graphs only.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is for unweighted regular MaxCut instances. It does not show an advantage over classical solvers in general.

assertions.value: The authors report that small-scale simulations show unit-depth XQAOA surpassing both QAOA and MA-QAOA at all tested depths up to five.
quotes: Small-scale simulations also reveal that unit-depth XQAOA invariably surpasses both QAOA and MA-QAOA on all tested depths up to five.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study. Small-scale simulations.

assertions.value: The authors state that they find an infinite family of graphs for which XQAOA solves MaxCut exactly, and show analytically that for some graphs in this family special cases of XQAOA achieve a much larger approximation ratio than QAOA.
quotes: we find an infinite family of graphs for which XQAOA solves MaxCut exactly and analytically show
for some graphs in this family, special cases of XQAOA are capable of achieving a much larger approximation ratio than QAOA
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytic result stated by the authors.
